I absolutely love crock pot cooking. What's your favorite meal to slow cook?
What's your favorite crock pot recipe?

Well, I'm a vegetarian (mostly - RE: Flexiterian) so I cook whatever recipe that has meat in it and substitute it for temp-ha or legumes. I haven't cooked anything in my slow-cooker recently, but this was the last thing I cooked (around the Holidays - 2014): Slow Cooker Spiced Bread Pudding Recipe

I love slow cooking for its flexibility. My old favorite recipe was:

  • 3-4 chicken breasts (or 6-8 boneless skinless thighs)
  • 1 jar of hot or medium salsa
  • 1 can of black beans
  • 1 can of corn

After it's all cooked, shred the chicken and mix everything in the slow cooker. Serve over rice with cheddar cheese on top.

When I started dieting I took out the beans and corn and added 1 cup of chicken broth. After that cooks I shred and mix before adding a few tablespoons of sour cream (I hear you can also use cream cheese or greek yogurt). Mix that in and let it cook for another 30 minutes and you've got a delicious creamy chicken soup.

I was actually planning on cooking this tonight, but at the last second I realized I forgot the salsa so tonight I'm trying it with stir-fry veggies plus chilli powder and cayenne pepper instead. And extra broth.

I often make a week's worth of steel cut oats on a Saturday night. Sunday morning is fresh oats for both my husband and myself. Then there are six servings left for me to heat in the microwave for the rest of the week. (My husband eats fruit and yogurt at his desk at work most of the rest of the week, or cold cereal.)

  • coconut oil cooking spray
  • 2 cups steel cut oats
  • 8 cups water

First I spray the inside of the crock with the cooking spray (it's an old crock, so no fancy non-stick surface here). Next I put in the water -- I believe all the people who complain that doing steel cut oats in the slow cooker just makes a caked-on sticky mess have this problem because they put the oats in first. By putting the water in first, all the oats are wet before they contact the crock. Having that film of water between the oats and the crock prevent it from forming a cement. Oats go in last. Salt is optional. I've done it with and without. I almost always salt my oats just before eating anyway (along w/ brown sugar and cinnamon). Leaving them plain lets me dress them up however I want during the week.

I cook on low overnight. They've usually cooked at least 8 hours or more by the time I get up for breakfast.

Another complaint I've seen about doing steel cut oats in the slow cooker is that they lose their chewy texture. That's true, especially with the very long cooking time that I use, but I don't mind how they come out.

This isn't really a meal (unless you have the flu), but I love to make broth/stock in the crock pot. Pile in your base (soup bones, a chicken carcass, fish heads, mushrooms, etc), onions, carrots, celery, and herbs/spices of your choice. Fill the crock with hot water and set to "high" until you get a simmer going, then switch to "low" and leave it overnight. Strain the broth, then either skim it or put it in the fridge until the fat solidifies on top. Discard (or save) fat, and then either use the broth in three days or freeze it. I like to freeze it in an ice cube tray and then put the cubes in a freezer bag so I can take out just what I need for one meal.

PS - the soup bones really benefit from browning in the oven first. Just hit them with some cooking spray and put them on a sheet at 500 until they get some good brown color on them.

Category: Science Fiction  

Short Synopsis:  

A young, androgynous Jedi named Amaranth (an Arkanian / Human hybrid individual), who has aged slowly due to his / her power of his / her own Midichlorins and knows both Sith and Jedi powers, seeks to destroy or at least corrupt Luke Skywalker and his son, Ben Skywalker (as well as Luke's other family members.) Amaranth has to develop powers on his / her own and in doing so, hides in the Outer Rim Territories to use both Jedi and Sith powers together, not aware that Anakin Skywalker had a son living on Tatooine. Amaranth is on a vengeful / revengeful path due to seeing his best friend murdered by the hands of Anakin Skywalker (the youngling who said, "Master Skywalker, There are too many of them!. What are we going to do?" in Star Wars III: Revenge of the Sith at the Jedi Temple destruction.) Amaranth was in the next room, deeply meditating, when the destruction of the temple began. Amaranth has tracked down Ben Skywalker and Luke, who are in exile, and catch up with them while they are discovering the Lost Tribe of Sith. Amaranth, having once been involved with the entity known as Abeloth in the Lost Tribe of Sith, searches out Luke and his son after nearly five decades of determination. And the story begins...  

Novel Excerpt:  

  • Amaranth speaking as the narrator while scoping out Ben in a nearby market:
  • "Is that him? He, whose grandfather destroyed my life. Does he even know? Does he even care? No matter. The pain in my mind replays over and over. Life is ever changing. So let life change again."
  • As Amaranth approaches Ben, Luke Skywalker suddenly, feeling a presence he has not felt since meeting his father for the first time in Episode V, shields his son from the would be mark of Amaranth's light-saber. A saber constructed on the fly, glowing blue and green, nearly at once.
  • "Who are you?" , demanded Luke.
  • Amaranth, knowing that Luke does not even know, remains silent and withdraws the blueish-greenish blade and the blade eventually dissolves into his / her left hand.
  • "Someone that knew your father for a brief time." "I've come to seek you two out."
  • "Seek who out and why?" asks Luke, very agitated and on edge, his blade also retracted.
  • "That answer may cost the life of your son. It already cost my best friends' life, by the hands of a Anakin Skywalker."
  • "You know of him, do you not?" Amaranth was sly and coy with his / her response with a slight smirk.
